answers.explanation: Amoeba and an unlaid egg (ovum) are each a single living cell.
Chlamydomonas and Euglena are flagellates that move using flagella.
Cell walls and chloroplasts occur only in plant cells, not in animal cells.
A flower with both stamens and pistil is described as perfect (hermaphrodite).
Mosquito larvae and pupae breathe air at the surface, so the oil film blocks air and suffocates them.
Evolutionary order runs from fish (IV) to amphibian (II) to bird (III) to mammal (I).
In the food web, the hawk feeds on lizards at the third level from vegetation, so it is a tertiary consumer.
Grasshopper and mouse both feed on vegetation, so they compete for the same food.
Opposable digits let a monkey grip branches, an adaptation to life in trees.
A community in which the same species persist from year to year is a stable climax vegetation.
Sexual intercourse is the most common route of AIDS transmission.
Efficient seed dispersal moves seeds away from the parent, reducing overcrowding.
Physical and climatic factors mainly determine which types of plants can grow in a region.
Each step in the flow of energy through an ecosystem is called a trophic level.
Density equals total count divided by total area: 48 divided by (20 x 2 m^2) = 1.2 per m^2.
Submerged water plants need little mechanical support, so their xylem supporting tissue is poorly developed.
Lime makes clay particles flocculate, opening the texture so excess water drains and waterlogging is prevented.
Agro-chemicals washed off farmland drain into and pollute fresh water sources.
A transect across a tropical rain forest records the greatest number of species because it is the most diverse habitat.
Darwin's natural selection implies that the organisms best adapted to their environment are the most successful.
Carnassial teeth for shearing flesh are formed by the last upper premolar and the first lower molar.
Worker bees and termites are sterile, so only reproductives breed in their caste systems.
Gill slits appear in the embryos of all these vertebrate groups, which is evidence of common ancestry.
Long legs, long neck and a long straight pointed beak are adaptations of fish-catching wading birds.
Rhizopus, housefly and Hydra all digest food outside their cells, releasing enzymes into a cavity or onto food.
Mammalian red blood cells are disc-shaped and lack a nucleus when mature.
Vertebrates possess an internal bony endoskeleton, unlike invertebrates.
Pitcher plants obtain nutrients by trapping and digesting insects, a heterotrophic mode of nutrition.
Caustic soda absorbs carbon dioxide, so the set-up shows that carbon dioxide is necessary for photosynthesis.
Fresh water is hypotonic to marine fish cells, so water enters by osmosis and the cells swell and burst.
The lungs and heart both lie in the anterior (thoracic) part of the mammalian body cavity.
A tapeworm obtains food from its host's intestine, which is parasitic nutrition.
The pancreas lies within the loop of the duodenum in mammals.
In a caryopsis (grain), the pericarp is fused with the seed coat and cannot be separated.
Margarine and butter are rich in fats, so an obese person should avoid them.
Tissue respiration breaks down food to release energy for the body's use.
Inbreeding of animals with the desirable large body size fixes that trait in the herd.
Body size, height, weight and colour vary in a continuous range rather than in distinct classes.
A boy with genotype YXn has only the recessive allele on his single X chromosome, so he is colour-blind.
Each birth is independent of earlier births, so the probability of a girl is one half.
Among heterozygous by heterozygous offspring, one in four (1 out of 4) shows the recessive phenotype.
